questions.question: 1. What is the primary disadvantage of a baseline SISO (Single-Input Single-Output) system in a flat fading channel?

answers.a: It has a very high Level Crossing Rate (LCR).
answers.b: It has a very long Average Fade Duration (ADF).
answers.c: It is highly susceptible to deep fades, leading to high outage probability.
answers.d: It cannot be used for high data rates.

questions.question: 2. What do both Selection Combining (SC) and Maximal-Ratio Combining (MRC) require at the receiver to provide diversity gain?

answers.b: Multiple receive antennas or signal paths.
answers.d: A perfect knowledge of the data being sent.

questions.question: 3. What is the primary implementation advantage of Selection Combining (SC) when compared to Maximal-Ratio Combining (MRC)?

answers.a: SC provides a higher signal-to-noise ratio.
answers.b: SC is much simpler, as it only needs to select one signal, not combine them.
answers.c: SC works better when the user is moving fast.

questions.question: 4. How does Maximal-Ratio Combining (MRC) achieve the best possible performance?

answers.a: It selects the two strongest signals and averages them.
answers.b: It inverts the phase of weak signals to cancel them.
answers.c: It aligns the phases of all signals and sums them, weighted by their strength.
answers.d: It switches between antennas at a very high speed.

questions.question: 5. If a mobile user increases their speed (e.g., from walking to driving), what is the most likely effect on the Level Crossing Rate (LCR)?
6. If a mobile user increases their speed, what is the corresponding effect on the Average Fade Duration (ADF)?

answers.d: The ADF will become infinitely long.

questions.question: 7. If the system's acceptable signal quality threshold is *raised* (i.e., a better signal is required), what happens to the outage probability?

answers.b: The outage probability stays the same.
answers.d: The outage probability depends only on the LCR.

questions.question: 8. How does receiver diversity (like SC or MRC) fundamentally reduce outage probability?

answers.a: It increases the total transmitted power from the base station.
answers.b: It makes the signal travel a shorter distance.
answers.c: It relies on the low probability that all receive paths are in a deep fade at the same time.
answers.d: It changes the flat fading into frequency-selective fading.

questions.question: 9. When comparing SC and MRC with the same number of receiver antennas, which statement is true regarding performance?

answers.a: SC always has a lower outage probability than MRC.
answers.b: MRC always has a lower outage probability than SC.
answers.c: SC and MRC always have the identical outage probability.
answers.d: SC is better for LCR, while MRC is better for ADF.

questions.question: 10. Compared to a single-antenna (SISO) system, what is the general effect of using either SC or MRC on the Average Fade Duration (ADF)?

answers.c: ADF is not affected by diversity.
answers.d: ADF becomes equal to the LCR.
